why: A Fenwick tree used to find the k-th free slot: processed in reverse, the last insertion's index is final, and each earlier photo takes the (index+1)-th slot still free. Binary descent on a Fenwick tree of free slots finds it in O(log n).
hints: Inserting into a Python list is O(n) per insert, O(n^2) total. Which photo's final position do you know for sure?
The last photo's index is its final position. Going backwards, photo i ends up in the (index[i] + 1)-th slot not yet taken by a later photo.
Keep a Fenwick tree of free slots (all 1). For each photo from last to first, find the k-th one by binary descent, place the photo there and set the slot to 0. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Repeated IDs are separate photos; work with positions, not IDs.
index[i] is zero-based, so look for the (index[i] + 1)-th free slot.
Build the all-ones Fenwick tree in O(n), or with n updates.
